question.worked_solution:
We have a product of a negative number and a positive number, so the product will be negative:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-\frac{4}{7})\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) & =-(\frac{4}{7}\cdot \frac{1}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply the fractions by multiplying the numerators and denominators separately:

$$
\begin{aligned}-(\frac{4}{7}\cdot \frac{1}{2}) & =-(\frac{4\cdot 1}{7\cdot 2}) \\  & =-(\frac{2\cdot 2\cdot 1}{7\cdot 2}) \\  & =-(\frac{2\cdot \cancel{2}\cdot 1}{7\cdot \cancel{2}}) \\  & =-(\frac{2}{7}) \\  & =-\frac{2}{7}\end{aligned}
$$
